limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

0inding F5 of NOTE-mvro4w8x (decisions GD-82, GD-83). The land gate (packages/runner/src/ticked-gate.ts) asks `GET /v1/runs/:id/tasks/:taskId/receipt-v2` BEFORE the land step runs. That route needs the fact "landing" (`landingOf` in packages/api/src/task-receipt-v2-facts.ts: a land step that waits on the integrate step which promoted the commit, whose output has outcome "landed"), and only the land step itself records that, after it has landed. So the gate refused every landing of work created after the ticked line (seen on 2026-10-28: run 01a180f0-577f-74de-9edd-a784cf36b900, task 01a180f0-e498-70b7-8d6e-7ff245695d20: "run ... did not record the landing of task ..., so no receipt is signed for it: it would be recorded in a land step that waits on the integrate step"). This task is the coordinator's half of the fix: an answer, without signing or recording anything, to "could this task's receipt be signed once its landing is recorded?". A later task makes the gate ask it.

THE CHANGE.
1. packages/api/src/task-receipt-v2-facts.ts: `receiptV2FactsOf(records, options?)` takes an optional `{ landing: 'pending' }`. With it, `landingOf` takes as the landing the LATEST land step that waits on the integrate step which promoted the delivered commit, whatever its output (it is the step now asking), and every other fact is gathered exactly as now, the acceptance being read on THAT step's ledger entry; when no land step waits on the integrate step it is the gap "landing" as now. Without the option nothing changes.
2. packages/api/src/task-receipt-v2-route.ts: a new route `GET /v1/runs/:id/tasks/:taskId/receipt-v2/ready` in `RECEIPT_V2_ROUTES` (packages/api/src/receipt-handlers.ts already spreads that list, so no other file registers it), policy READER. It reads the run the way `handleGetTaskReceiptV2` does (share that reading code, do not copy it), calls `receiptV2FactsOf` with the option, and answers 200 `{ ready: true, run_id, task_id }` when the facts are gathered; otherwise the SAME refusals the receipt route gives for the same cause (404 for an unknown task, 409 API_RECEIPT_V2_FACT_MISSING naming the fact, the failed-check refusal as it is). It signs nothing, records nothing, needs no signing key, never calls `changeState`, and a receipt already recorded changes nothing about it. A ready answer is NOT a receipt: nothing in its body may look like one (no signature, no receipt schema).

TESTS, in a NEW file packages/api/src/task-receipt-v2-ready.test.ts (under 500 lines, module comment 25 lines or fewer), built on real facts as task-receipt-v2-facts.test.ts and task-receipt-v2-route.test-support.ts build them (extend that test-support file if you need to). Cover: ready when the work order, the delivered commit, the promoted integration, the delivery, the check records and the acceptance on the land step are all recorded and the land step has not landed (ready or running); the SAME records make the receipt route refuse with the fact "landing" (this is the flaw: assert it); not ready without a work order; without a promoted integrate step; with an acceptance by someone other than the order's acceptor; with a failed check; with no land step; unknown task is 404; no event is written by a ready answer (compare the event count) and no receipt is recorded by it; after the landing is recorded the ready answer still holds. Each assertion must be able to fail: change the code to check.

CONSTRAINTS. Existing tests are edited only where this change breaks them, and the report lists them. Module comments of existing files may not grow. A source file stays under 500 lines (task-receipt-v2-route.ts is 361, task-receipt-v2-facts.ts 369). Touch no other file.
